resources.string: Plays from Spotify, Apple Music and YouTube Music exports
Ask a service for a copy of your data, then pick the zip or files it sends you. Aurora adds exactly what the export lists: it never guesses play times, albums, artists or places.

On Spotify\'s privacy page, ask for Extended streaming history (everything since your account began, can take up to 30 days) or Account data (about the last year, usually within 5 days). Pick the zip Spotify emails you, or the Streaming_History_Audio or StreamingHistory_music files inside it.

On privacy.apple.com choose Request a copy of your data and tick Apple Media Services information. Pick the zip Apple sends you. Newer exports name no artist next to each play, so Aurora takes it from the same zip\'s daily track list or library where those name exactly one; otherwise the play keeps no artist.

In Google Takeout, select only YouTube and YouTube Music, include only history, and set the history format to JSON. Pick the Takeout zip or watch-history.json. YouTube\'s history states no play length, so those plays count as plays but add no minutes.
A zip, JSON, CSV or HTML file. You can pick several at once.
Without a stated play length: %1$s. They count as plays, not as minutes.
Without an artist in the export: %1$s. They count towards songs and albums, not artists.
These files hold no music plays to add.
This removes the plays this import added. Aurora\'s own plays and your other imports stay.
Detailed statistics are on, so imported plays with a stated length go into them too. Time of day comes from the export\'s own timestamps; device, sound and places stay empty.
